text:
Dear Principal,

I am writing to urge you to adopt the all-day phone ban, including lunch. I believe it would do more for our students than a ban limited to class time.

A class-only ban leaves students with phones for the rest of the day, and that is when the phones cause the most trouble. Lunch and passing periods are the only times students can talk face to face without a teacher directing the conversation. If most of them spend those minutes looking at screens, they miss the chance to build friendships, practice conversation and rest their minds. A student who sits alone with a phone at lunch can go the whole day without speaking to a classmate.

Phones also make a class-only ban hard to enforce. Teachers must spot hidden phones, argue with students and sometimes stop teaching to deal with them. Students who have been scrolling through lunch also bring that habit into class, and what they saw online follows them. A fight started in a group chat, a rumor or an embarrassing video can spill into the next period. With an all-day rule, teachers don't have to judge each case. The rule is the same in every room and at every hour, so students know what to expect and staff don't have to improvise.

Some families will object that they need to reach their children during the day. That concern is fair, and the school can answer it. Parents can call the front office, and staff can pass urgent messages to students quickly. Students who need a phone for a medical reason should get an exception. These steps address the concern without leaving every phone in every pocket.

Others will say lunch is free time and students should be able to spend it as they like. I understand that. But lunch is also one of the few chances in the day for students to talk, play and move around, and phones crowd out all three. Many schools that have tried full-day bans report livelier cafeterias and fewer conflicts that begin online. I would encourage us to ask nearby schools about their results before we decide.

For these reasons, I ask you to adopt the ban for the whole school day. If the rollout goes well, we can review it after one semester and adjust whatever is not working.

Thank you for considering this.

Sincerely,
[Your name]
